[bold #D75FFF]◆ EPIC sase-sq.7.1[/bold #D75FFF]
[dim]  Title: [bold #D7AFFF][/dim]Glossary migration to a core web[/bold #D7AFFF]
[dim]   Goal: [#D7D7AF][/dim]The `sase` and `bob-cli` glossaries stop living in [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]`memory.glossary` and become file-backed core memory webs: [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]`sase/memory/glossary.md` is a user-owned descriptor with a managed[/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]roster region, each term is a strand file under [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]`sase/memory/glossary/`, the Rust glossary source wire addresses [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]strand files so editor go-to-definition lands on a real Markdown [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]note, config and files can never both be live, and `sase glossary [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]*` survives one release as a deprecating alias over `sase memory`.[/#D7D7AF]
[dim] Counts: [bold #D7AFFF][/dim]6[dim][/bold #D7AFFF] phases[dim][/dim] · [bold #D7AFFF][/dim]4[dim][/bold #D7AFFF] waves[/dim]

[dim]  1 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]File-backed glossary source wire[/bold #D7AFFF]                              [bold black on #FFD75F] medium [/bold black on #FFD75F]
    [#AF87FF]wire[dim] · [dim][/dim]no dependencies[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]wire: generalize sase-core's GlossarySourceWire from [/#D7D7AF]

    [#D7D7AF]adapter and its readers to emit new names and accept both.[/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  2 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Inline roster parity with the generated glossary note[/bold #D7AFFF]         [bold black on #87D7FF] small  [/bold black on #87D7FF]
    [#AF87FF]roster[dim] · [dim][/dim]no dependencies[/#AF87FF][/dim]

    [#D7D7AF]instead of configured aliases, Markdown escaping, and wrapping at the [/#D7D7AF]

    [#AF87FF]source[dim] · [dim][/dim]after wire[/#AF87FF][/dim]

    [#D7D7AF]source ranges, make editor_glossary_catalog_for_project and [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]load_project_glossary_terms prefer the web and fail closed when config [/#D7D7AF]

[dim]  4 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]The sase memory web migrate command[/bold #D7AFFF]                           [bold black on #FFD75F] medium [/bold black on #FFD75F]
    [#AF87FF]migrate[dim] · [dim][/dim]after roster, source[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]migrate: add `sase memory web migrate glossary [-n] [-p REF]`, which [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]writes one strand per configured term, removes the memory.glossary block[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]with a source-preserving YAML edit, and rewrites sase/memory/glossary.md[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]as a user-owned web descriptor.[/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  5 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]sase glossary as a deprecating alias[/bold #D7AFFF]                          [bold black on #FFD75F] medium [/bold black on #FFD75F]
    [#AF87FF]compat[dim] · [dim][/dim]after source[/#AF87FF][/dim]

    [#D7D7AF]deprecation notice naming its `sase memory` equivalent and delegate to [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]it when the project has a glossary web, and make `sase glossary add|del`[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]write and delete strand files instead of config entries when the web [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]exists.[/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  6 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Migrate the sase and bob-cli trees[/bold #D7AFFF]                            [bold black on #FFD75F] medium [/bold black on #FFD75F]
    [#AF87FF]trees[dim] · [dim][/dim]after compat, migrate[/#AF87FF][/dim]

    [#D7D7AF]closures match, and `sase memory init --check` is clean for sase, [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]bob-cli, and home.[/#D7D7AF]
